title: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Kings 25](/bible/2-kings/25)

**[2 Kings 25:1-3](/bible/2-kings/25#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-kings/25#v1)</sup> And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he, and all his host, against Jerusalem, and pitched against it; and they built forts against it round about.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-kings/25#v2)</sup> And the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-kings/25#v3)</sup> And on the ninth day of the fourth month the famine prevailed in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

- In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign Nebuchadnezzar came with all his host against Jerusalem, pitched against it, and built forts round about it.
- The city was besieged until the eleventh year of Zedekiah, and the famine prevailed in the city.
- Because the city was besieged no food, water, or goods could get in, so there was no bread for the people of the land.

**[2 Kings 25:4-7](/bible/2-kings/25#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/2-kings/25#v4)</sup> And the city was broken up, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls, which is by the king’s garden: (now the Chaldees were against the city round about:) and the king went the way toward the plain.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/2-kings/25#v5)</sup> And the army of the Chaldees pursued after the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho: and all his army were scattered from him.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/2-kings/25#v6)</sup> So they took the king, and brought him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah; and they gave judgment upon him.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-kings/25#v7)</sup> And they slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon.

- The city was broken up and the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were round about the city.
- The army pursued the king, overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and his army was scattered from him, and they took him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where judgment was given upon him.
- They slew Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, then put out his eyes, bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon, just as Jeremiah had warned him.

**[2 Kings 25:8-12](/bible/2-kings/25#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/2-kings/25#v8)</sup> And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which is the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzar–adan, captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, unto Jerusalem:
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-kings/25#v9)</sup> And he burnt the house of the Lord, and the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great man’s house burnt he with fire.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-kings/25#v10)</sup> And all the army of the Chaldees, that were with the captain of the guard, brake down the walls of Jerusalem round about.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/2-kings/25#v11)</sup> Now the rest of the people that were left in the city, and the fugitives that fell away to the king of Babylon, with the remnant of the multitude, did Nebuzar–adan the captain of the guard carry away.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-kings/25#v12)</sup> But the captain of the guard left of the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen.

- In the fifth month of the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard came to Jerusalem.
- He burnt the house of the Lord, the king's house, and every great man's house, and the army broke down the walls of Jerusalem round about.
- He carried away the rest of the people and the fugitives, but left the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen, since the poor could not fend for themselves.

**[2 Kings 25:13-17](/bible/2-kings/25#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/2-kings/25#v13)</sup> And the pillars of brass that were in the house of the Lord, and the bases, and the brasen sea that was in the house of the Lord, did the Chaldees break in pieces, and carried the brass of them to Babylon.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-kings/25#v14)</sup> And the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass wherewith they ministered, took they away.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/2-kings/25#v15)</sup> And the firepans, and the bowls, and such things as were of gold, in gold, and of silver, in silver, the captain of the guard took away.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-kings/25#v16)</sup> The two pillars, one sea, and the bases which Solomon had made for the house of the Lord; the brass of all these vessels was without weight.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/2-kings/25#v17)</sup> The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and the chapiter upon it was brass: and the height of the chapiter three cubits; and the wreathen work, and pomegranates upon the chapiter round about, all of brass: and like unto these had the second pillar with wreathen work.

- The Chaldeans broke in pieces the pillars of brass, the bases, and the brasen sea that were in the house of the Lord, and carried the brass to Babylon because it was valuable.
- They took away the pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and vessels of brass, and the firepans and bowls of gold and silver the captain of the guard took away.
- The two pillars, one sea, and the bases Solomon had made were of brass without weight, the one pillar eighteen cubits high with a brasen chapiter, wreathen work, and pomegranates round about.

**[2 Kings 25:18-21](/bible/2-kings/25#v18)**

> <sup>[18](/bible/2-kings/25#v18)</sup> And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door:
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/2-kings/25#v19)</sup> And out of the city he took an officer that was set over the men of war, and five men of them that were in the king’s presence, which were found in the city, and the principal scribe of the host, which mustered the people of the land, and threescore men of the people of the land that were found in the city:
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-kings/25#v20)</sup> And Nebuzar–adan captain of the guard took these, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah:
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/2-kings/25#v21)</sup> And the king of Babylon smote them, and slew them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried away out of their land.

- The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door.
- He took an officer over the men of war, five men in the king's presence, the principal scribe of the host, and threescore men of the people found in the city.
- Nebuzaradan brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and the king smote and slew them there; so Judah was carried away out of their land.

**[2 Kings 25:22-26](/bible/2-kings/25#v22)**

> <sup>[22](/bible/2-kings/25#v22)</sup> And as for the people that remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, even over them he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, ruler.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/2-kings/25#v23)</sup> And when all the captains of the armies, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor, there came to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan the son of Careah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of a Maachathite, they and their men.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/2-kings/25#v24)</sup> And Gedaliah sware to them, and to their men, and said unto them, Fear not to be the servants of the Chaldees: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon; and it shall be well with you.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/2-kings/25#v25)</sup> But it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, came, and ten men with him, and smote Gedaliah, that he died, and the Jews and the Chaldees that were with him at Mizpah.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/2-kings/25#v26)</sup> And all the people, both small and great, and the captains of the armies, arose, and came to Egypt: for they were afraid of the Chaldees.

- Over the people left in the land Nebuchadnezzar made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor.
- Gedaliah counselled the captains and their men not to fear to serve the Chaldeans but to dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it would be well with them.
- But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the royal seed, came with ten men and smote Gedaliah and the Jews and Chaldeans with him, and the people fled to Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans, killing a man who gave wise counsel.

**[2 Kings 25:27-30](/bible/2-kings/25#v27)**

> <sup>[27](/bible/2-kings/25#v27)</sup> And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the seven and twentieth day of the month, that Evil–merodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison;
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/2-kings/25#v28)</sup> And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon;
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/2-kings/25#v29)</sup> And changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/2-kings/25#v30)</sup> And his allowance was a continual allowance given him of the king, a daily rate for every day, all the days of his life.

- In the thirty seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin, Evilmerodach king of Babylon lifted up his head out of prison and spake kindly to him.
- He set his throne above the thrones of the other kings in Babylon, changed his prison garments, and let him eat bread continually before him all the days of his life.
- Jehoiachin was given a continual daily allowance for the rest of his life, a mercy shown at the very end of the account.
